evidence_class: CONTAINER EVIDENCE, NOT PRODUCTION. Same throwaway Docker method as tools/server-performance-qualification.json (compose project hmem-perftest, loopback only); the live system was not contacted.
outcome: PARTIAL: replay reads are ordered index range scans in every plan and their statement time falls from about 0.8 s (before) and 67-74 s (073d6bfb after) to 0.13-0.23 s per contention phase. Pooled foreground p95 and seeded capture append pass the 10% gate for both variants, but 7 of 10 ordinary routes still regress 1.3-3.6x at p95, so the per-route gate and task acceptance fail. The skip removes idle outbox reads and 81-86% of contention reads without changing foreground latency, so the remaining regression is not caused by outbox scans.

change.a_predicate: hmem-core/src/HMem/DB/ChangeStream.hs: listOutboxAfterStatement and listOutboxRangeStatement filter coalesce(workspace_id, zero) = coalesce($2, zero), the uq_change_stream_global_cursor expression, instead of workspace_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2. No migration.
change.b_skip: hmem-server/src/HMem/Server/ChangeStream.hs: the dispatcher reads the rotated scopes with their committed next_cursor (listDispatchScopes) and skips listOutboxAfter when the counter is not past the process acknowledgement. After a successfully dispatched turn a read shorter than 1,000 records acknowledges max(last record, observed counter) and a full read its last record; a failed turn keeps every acknowledgement. DispatchBatchRead still lists every rotated scope; DispatchScopesScanned names the scopes read. Per-socket replay is unchanged.

method.measurement: Client latency from the host. Database counts are pg_stat_statements calls per phase: outbox_scan = statements containing FROM change_stream_outbox, scope_lock = hmem_change_stream_lock. Pool wait share = mean db_wait_ms / mean complete_ms over the slowest 5% of joined foreground requests; the before image has no request phases or pool counters.

findings: The predicate repair removes the replay scan cost: about 13-16k outbox reads per contention phase take 0.20-0.23 s in total, against 67-74 s for 7.1-7.8k reads in the 073d6bfb after runs, and pooled foreground p95 falls to within 3.2% of before.

The dispatcher skip removes every idle outbox read (668-692 per 30 s with a alone) and 81-86% of contention reads, but foreground latency does not improve (a+b pooled 1.093 against a 1.032, inside the 9.7% spread between the two before runs). Outbox reads no longer explain the regression.

Cheap reads still regress 2-3.6x at p95 (task_get 7.6 to 19-27 ms, planning_counts 7.7 to 24-27 ms) while database work per statement is unchanged: the after images run the same statement mix (2.19-2.40M calls per phase against 2.22-2.26M) and 35-42% of the foreground tail is pool wait, with 13.6-15.9k capacity waits and 173-223 s of total wait per phase.

The largest remaining change-stream database difference is scope locking: 3,053-5,113 hmem_change_stream_lock calls taking 6.9-10.3 s per contention phase against 255-271 calls and 0.5 s before. These come from per-socket canonical delivery and replay, which this task left unchanged; on one-connection pool stripes their lock waits behind hot writers are the leading candidate for the remaining queueing, not yet isolated.

Delivery is unchanged by the skip: every healthy hot observer received every hot change (ab-2 counted 1,911 of 1,920 because its contention phase ended 0.3 s after the 120 s write window while delivery takes about 1 s; all four observers stopped at the same count), commit-to-frame p95 0.93-0.96 s; before delivered 233-250 of 1,920 beside the stalled reader.
Memory peaks at 338-359 MiB for the after variants against 409-428 MiB before.
limitations: Two runs per variant on one shared host; the before runs differ by 9.7% pooled p95 (87.8 and 96.3 ms). The a+b pooled ratio of 1.093 is within that spread of the limit.
The unfixed after image (d4d70f78 without these changes) was not rerun on this seed; comparisons with it use the 073d6bfb receipt, which had a different seed copy and its load-profile history.
Foreground clients are closed-loop, so before completed 7% (against a) and 10% (against a+b) more foreground requests on average; hot writes were open-loop and matched.
The before image's scratch Dockerfile was reconstructed and is not byte-identical to the 073d6bfb one; image content was not compared.
The before image has no request phases or pool counters, so pool wait share is reported for after variants only.
Local authentication makes every principal the trusted superadmin; revocation and per-user reauthorization rely on the focused specs.
